lifetime.question: Tick all the situations that apply or have applied to you.
lifetime.why: Some people cannot give blood because it would be risky for them or for others.

health.question: Are you generally in good health, with no cold or fever symptoms?
health.why: Better safe than sorry! We prefer people with mild symptoms to recover fully before donating.

medication.question: Have you taken any medication in the last 4 weeks?
medication.why: Some medications can make blood donation unsafe, risking harm to the recipient or the donor.

travel.question: If you've travelled in the last 6 months, where did you go?
travel.why: In some parts of the world, pathogens can travel back with you and only become detectable up to 6 months later!

partner.question: Have you had several sexual partners in the last 12 months, or changed partner in the last 4 months?
partner.why: It's personal, but important for minimising the risk of transmitting an STI to the recipient.

hospitalization.question: What is the most serious hospitalisation you've had recently?
hospitalization.why: Someone recovering from major surgery or childbirth needs time to recover before donating.

recent.response: A&E / consultation less than 4 weeks ago

admission.response: Hospital admission in the last year

dentist.question: What is the most intensive dental treatment you've had recently?
dentist.why: These treatments cause small lesions through which bacteria or viruses can enter and contaminate the blood.

extraction.response: Extraction less than a week ago

complications.response: Extraction with complications less than two weeks ago

tattoo.question: Select the styles you've added in the last 4 months
tattoo.why: These can cause small wounds that open the door to bacteria and viruses.

none.response: None, I'm perfect as I am 😎

tick.question: Did you come back from an outdoor walk with a little companion in the last 4 weeks?
tick.why: Ticks, like mosquitoes, carry diseases (such as Lyme disease) transmitted through their bacteria. Check your whole body after a walk in nature.

vaccine.question: Tick any vaccines you've received recently.
vaccine.why: Depending on the vaccine type, a waiting period may be required to avoid transmitting a live attenuated virus, or simply to ensure you have no side effects. In most cases, vaccination doesn't prevent donation.

live.response: Live attenuated vaccine less than 4 months ago

inactivated.response: Inactivated/mRNA vaccine less than 48 h ago

unknown.response: I don't know the type but it was less than 4 months ago

faq.a1: Eat and drink well before coming, avoid alcohol and bring an ID document.
faq.a2: A confidential interview precedes the donation, which lasts about 10 minutes. A snack is offered afterwards.
faq.a3: Allow about 45 minutes in total, including check-in, interview, donation and rest time.
faq.q4: Can I donate if I take medication?
faq.a4: It depends on the treatment. The eligibility test and the on-site medical interview will confirm it.
faq.a5: You only feel a slight prick when the needle is inserted. The donation itself is painless.
faq.a6: Men can donate up to 4 times a year and women up to 3 times, with a minimum of 3 months between two donations.
faq.q7: What happens to the donated blood?
faq.a7: The blood is tested, prepared and distributed to hospitals for patients who need it: emergencies, surgeries, cancer treatments.
faq.q8: Do I need to register in advance?
faq.a8: Booking an appointment is recommended to reduce waiting time, but you can also drop in during the drive's opening hours.

histoire.title: An idea born in 2008, relaunched in 2026
histoire.p1: The Generosity Trophy was conceived in 2008 by the HUG Blood Transfusion Centre to recognise Geneva companies that organise blood drives and mobilise the most donors.
histoire.p2: After three successful editions (2008, 2009, 2010), the project was put on hold due to a lack of resources to sustain it.
histoire.p3: In 2026, in partnership with HEIG-VD and thanks to a dedicated digital platform, the Trophy is officially relaunched - more ambitious, more accessible, and open to all companies in French-speaking Switzerland.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.q1: How do I organise a blood drive at my company?
faq.a1: Contact the HUG Blood Transfusion Centre via the registration form. A team will guide you through planning the date, venue and internal communications.
faq.a2: The Generosity Trophy is an annual award for companies that mobilise the most donors during their blood drives. Launched in 2008, it has been reactivated to recognise the commitment of partner companies.
faq.a3: Any company that has organised at least one blood drive with HUG during the current year can compete for the Trophy, regardless of its size.
faq.q4: What is the CTS CSR Label?
faq.a4: The CTS CSR Label is a certification awarded by the Blood Transfusion Centre to companies that sustainably integrate blood donation into their corporate social responsibility policy. It is renewable each year.
faq.q5: How do I know if I am eligible to donate blood?
faq.a5: Use our interactive 'Am I eligible?' journey to quickly check your eligibility. If in doubt, the HUG teams are available to answer your questions.
